modules.purpose: Monte-Carlo propagation of a shock through the causal (`influences`) layer of the graph. For every reachable component reports three parallel figures per path: the exact composed (unattenuated) elasticity product, the depth-attenuated version, and a seeded Monte-Carlo sample, plus a noisy-OR combined figure across paths that share edges (dependence handled structurally).
modules.key_functions: schedule()/factor()/pin()/published() load+validate attenuation.yaml; _edge_draws() draws one PERT stream per edge (shared across paths); _path_entry() builds composed/attenuated/sampled triple per path and applies the may_price gate; _expected_product() computes E[prod] analytically incl. raw moments for repeated edges; _joint() combines paths by noisy-OR with exact inclusion-exclusion up to MAX_EXACT_PATHS=10 and reports if_independent vs exact (double_counting_avoided); propagate() is the entry point doing BFS/DFS walk (max_depth=5, max_paths=32) and assembling the closed artefact body; refuse_undeclared_keys()/refuse_directional_magnitudes() are structural closure guards.
modules.depends_on: twin/attenuation.yaml (schedule), twin/pert.py (Triple, PERT sampler, quantise, summarise, procedure), twin/evidence.py (pricing threshold/gating), twin/canon.py (digest, walk_keys), twin/schema.py (CAUSAL_EDGE, SIGNS), twin/model.py (Graph/Edge, at runtime), twin/artefact.py (ArtefactError)

modules.purpose: Versioned data file: the depth-decay schedule that scales composed causal influence by hop depth, and the boundary past which a result becomes directional-only (no magnitude).
modules.key_functions: n/a (data). schema twin.attenuation/v1, version 1. directional_beyond_depth: 4. factors depth 1-4: 1.0, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, each with a `because` rationale string.

modules.purpose: Reverse-dependency blast radius: from an origin, walk both causal (`influences`, forward) and structural (`needs`, backward) edges to find every downstream-affected component, classifying each as priced, below-threshold, or no-mechanism (structural-only, unpriced by design).
modules.key_functions: classify() decides priced/BELOW_THRESHOLD/NO_MECHANISM per path; radius() does the DFS walk (max_depth=6) tracking best (Reached) per component by rank, splits results into admitted_to_pricing vs unpriced; Reached.rank orders priced > claimed-but-weak > structural-only, then shorter/better-evidenced/lexicographic; refuse_undeclared_keys() closes the body schema (no price/cost/loss/severity field exists at all).
modules.depends_on: twin/evidence.py (threshold, published), twin/schema.py (CAUSAL_EDGE, STRUCTURAL_EDGE), twin/canon.py (walk_keys), twin/artefact.py (ArtefactError), twin/model.py (Graph/Edge). Explicitly inherited algorithm/limits from /arckit:impact plugin.

modules.purpose: The `causal-claims` skill: given free-text evidence about a claimed relationship between two components, proposes a causal edge (sign, lag, elasticity range, evidence grade) and a mandatory alternative-explanations field, plus a structural one-hop confounder detector. Also defines two separately-thresholded scoring metrics (claim accuracy vs. grade accuracy, asymmetrically penalised) and a labelled corpus.
modules.key_functions: shared_ancestors() — the free structural confounder detector, one-hop only; _sign()/_grade()/_lag_days()/_elasticity() — keyword-heuristic classifiers; _alternatives() — always includes reverse-causation plus one entry per flagged confounder; propose() — the skill entry point; scorer()/grade_scorer() — claim-accuracy (sign/lag/elasticity tolerance) vs grade-accuracy with zero tolerance for over-grading and 1-rung tolerance for under-grading; labelled_corpus() builds 4 items from the netflix/intel fixture read back through Overlay.
modules.depends_on: twin/fixtures.py (netflix/intel org builders), twin/evidence.py (pricing_threshold), twin/model.py (Graph, Overlay), twin/repo.py (ModelRepo), twin/schema.py (CAUSAL_EDGE)

modules.purpose: Rival causal accounts (alternative graphs of `influences` edges for the same org) treated as unprivileged, like twin/positions.py does for rival world models. Propagates a shock independently under each named account and reports the spread of the primary path's attenuated mean at every reached component.
modules.key_functions: _primary_mean() extracts the primary path's attenuated mean (None past attenuation boundary); ensemble_spread() runs propagate.propagate() once per account, unmodified, and computes min/max/range/by_account spread per component; requires >=2 accounts.

modules.purpose: Pearl's counterfactual algorithm building blocks: Do (intervention, downstream-only propagation, incoming edges reported as severed) and Observe (bidirectional belief update) as two distinct dataclass types (not a boolean flag) plus `rewind()` (abduction: open the model repo at a past commit, a real state not a filtered view).
modules.key_functions: severed() — incoming causal edges cut by do(), type-guarded to Do only; _ancestor_paths() — BFS shortest causal ancestor path per node (linear cost, replaces exponential simple-path enumeration), bounded by UPSTREAM_MAX_DEPTH=5; updated_beliefs() — ancestors an Observe updates, directional-only (no magnitude, since inverting an elasticity needs an unauthored prior); refuse_upstream_under_intervention() — structural guard that an intervention never carries upstream updates; rewind() — ModelRepo.open_at_time(), fails explicitly before model existed.
modules.depends_on: twin/repo.py (ModelRepo, RepoError), twin/schema.py (CAUSAL_EDGE), twin/model.py (Edge/Graph at type-check time), twin/artefact.py (ArtefactError, lazily imported)

modules.purpose: The Wardley evolution-axis maths: stage banding and the D (differentiation pressure), K (commodity leverage), R (dependency risk) relations, plus a Position dataclass and a text-plot renderer. Explicitly ported (not rebuilt) from the installed arckit plugin, with arckit's action bands and £ prose deliberately excluded.
modules.key_functions: stage_of()/band()/midpoint() — banding logic (genesis/custom-built/product/commodity); differentiation_pressure()/commodity_leverage()/dependency_risk() — the three exact float formulas (D, K, R) with no quantisation, bit-identical arithmetic; Position.of()/positions() — build positions only where authored (never guessed); map_of() — builds the whole Wardley map + dependency-risk-per-structural-edge derived from the graph, no separate authoring step, lists unpositioned components/edges rather than dropping them; plot() renders a text grid purely from map_of()'s own output.
modules.depends_on: no other twin modules imported at module scope (schema.py imports wardley for band checks, so wardley avoids importing schema back to prevent a cycle)

modules.purpose: Believed/rival/revealed world models held as unprivileged named position sets, with computed (not merely displayed) pairwise deltas and proper-scoring-rule comparison against revealed truth.
modules.key_functions: _belief() reads one proposition's probability from a world model; revealed() derives ground truth from a resolved outcome (never authored as belief); pairwise_deltas() — |a-b| magnitude for every unordered pair; against_revealed() — delta plus scoring.score() (Brier/log-loss) against revealed truth; deltas() — top-level: gathers named positions, abstains where a model holds no belief, refuses if none hold one.

modules.purpose: The `evolution-judge` skill: infers a component's Wardley evolution position from accumulated evidence (grade-5 model assertion), accepts a human override (grade-4 calibrated judgement, attributable to a registered role), and generates a `pushback()` statement comparing the two (never silent, even on agreement).
modules.key_functions: _infer_position() — keyword-lookup heuristic fitted to 4 backtest orgs; judge() — the skill entry point, returns a claim-shaped dict with hardcoded evidence_grade=5; override() — requires the prior inferred claim for the same component, hardcodes grade=4; pushback() — compares inferred vs override position with a 0.1 agreement tolerance and always returns a statement; scorer() — tolerance-based (0.15) position scorer; labelled_corpus() — 4 items, one per backtest org (Carillion/NMC/Wirecard/Enron), each a single hardcoded expected evolution_position.
modules.depends_on: twin/wardley.py (stage_of), twin/fixtures.py (4 backtest org builders), twin/model.py (Overlay), twin/repo.py (ModelRepo)

modules.purpose: The `gameplay-lens` skill: checks two Wardley gameplay-pattern preconditions (land-grab, exploit-commoditisation) against the current map, deterministically, and a scheduled sweep() that scans every org's map on every run (the 'opportunities are pulled' counterweight to signals being pushed).
modules.key_functions: _land_grab()/_exploit_commoditisation() — precondition checks over position/needs-edges/ownership-edges; propose() — the skill entry point iterating org_components x PLAYS; sweep() — scheduled scan across repos/orgs producing an Artefact (KIND_OPPORTUNITY_SWEEP), reporting opportunity count beside signal count; labelled_corpus() — 3 fixture orgs (netflix land-grab positive, intel negative, pocket exploit-commoditisation positive).
modules.depends_on: twin/wardley.py (band constants via positions), twin/fixtures.py, twin/artefact.py (Artefact, DERIVED), twin/grades.py (Capabilities), twin/model.py (Overlay, orgs), twin/repo.py (ModelRepo), twin/schema.py (PERSON_EDGES, STRUCTURAL_EDGE), twin/TOOL_VERSION

modules.purpose: Anchors/reconciles a generated synthetic substrate against the org's own real, dated `signal` documents (the 'spine' of ground truth) to detect over-anchoring (rigged tests) and silent drift (unrecorded contradiction).
modules.key_functions: Spine.from_overlay() — builds the spine directly from overlay.signals (no second authored format); Spine.at() — knowability filter reusing regimes.cutoff(); anchor() — additive insertion of knowable facts into a batch channel, non-mutating; reconcile()/reconcile_at_every_checkpoint() — verifies every knowable fact is present verbatim, refuses naming what's missing; diff_against_spine() — splits substrate lines into anchored vs free_running, the named attack surface.

modules.purpose: Diffs one named scenario between two git refs: scalar/list field-level diff of the scenario's own declared fields, plus a map-diff (positions moved/added/removed) computed from Graph.wardley() at each ref.
modules.key_functions: _side() opens a ModelRepo at a given ref and loads the scenario (or None if absent); _scenario_fields() diffs scalar (before/after) and list (added/removed) fields; _map_diff() compares wardley() positions dict for stage/evolution changes; diff() — top-level entry building a DERIVED Artefact; refuses only if the scenario is absent at both refs.
modules.depends_on: twin/model.py (Overlay), twin/repo.py (ModelRepo, RepoError), twin/artefact.py (Artefact, DERIVED), twin/grades.py (Capabilities), twin/TOOL_VERSION

notes: This cluster is the causal/Wardley reasoning core of the twin, sitting above twin/model.py (Graph/Overlay/Edge) and twin/pert.py (PERT sampling primitives), and below twin/skills.py (the seam that runs skill_fn callables like causal_claims.propose, evolution_judge.judge/override, gameplay_lens.propose against labelled corpora with pass/fail thresholds). Three of the fifteen modules (causal_claims.py, evolution_judge.py, gameplay_lens.py) are explicitly self-described 'skills' whose classification logic is a small keyword heuristic standing in for a future model call — each says so in its own module docstring and marks the exact lines with a `ponytail:` comment, and each states the same upgrade path: swap the heuristic body for a model call with no change to the harness, tests, or callers, because the skill contract is a bare callable. The propagation/dependence machinery (propagate.py, blast.py, causal_accounts.py) and the maths/data modules (wardley.py, positions.py, evidence.py, evidence-ladder.yaml, attenuation.yaml) are genuine deterministic algorithms with dedicated, non-trivial test coverage exercising the actual numeric properties claimed (sub-additivity, exact-vs-sampled agreement, reproducibility, gate consistency). Two modules (spine.py, challenges.py) implement structural governance/audit mechanisms (fact reconciliation against a real git-derived spine; claim-path-scoped contestability) rather than statistical/optimisation algorithms, and both are exercised against real fixture data (the Carillion backtest for spine.py) rather than only synthetic inputs.
